photos.question: A client taking warfarin asks about diet. Which instruction should the nurse give?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #294!

🥬 Warfarin and leafy greens. Do you have to give up salad?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Keep vitamin K intake consistent

🧠 Rationale: Vitamin K reverses the effect of warfarin.

Clients do not need to avoid greens. Big changes in intake make the INR swing.

Steady, consistent intake keeps the dose working the same way each day.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Warfarin (Coumadin)

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 Oral anticoagulant (vitamin K antagonist)

📊 Lab to Monitor:

🔹 PT/INR, usual goal 2 to 3 for most clients

⚠️ Signs of Bleeding:

🔹 Bleeding gums or nosebleeds

🔹 Black, tarry stools

🔹 Blood in urine

🔹 Easy bruising

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Keep vitamin K foods steady

✅ Use a soft toothbrush and electric razor

✅ Avoid aspirin and NSAIDs unless approved

✅ Wear a medical alert ID

🚑 Antidote:

🔹 Vitamin K (phytonadione)

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Warfarin likes routine: same greens, same INR!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: Which ECG change should the nurse recognize as a sign of an acute myocardial infarction (STEMI)?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #295!

❤️ One ECG change that means time is muscle. Can you spot it?

This is a HIGH-YIELD cardiac question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — ST-segment elevation

🧠 Rationale: ST elevation shows acute injury to the heart muscle.

Peaked T waves point to high potassium. Sawtooth waves mean atrial flutter.

Prominent U waves point to low potassium.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Myocardial Infarction

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Crushing chest pain or pressure

🔹 Pain to jaw, neck or left arm

🔹 Shortness of breath and sweating

🔹 Women may have fatigue or nausea

📊 Diagnostics:

🔹 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes

🔹 Troponin is the most specific lab

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Get a 12-lead ECG right away

✅ Give aspirin as ordered

✅ Oxygen if SpO2 is below 90%

✅ Nitroglycerin and pain control as ordered

🚑 Emergency:

🔹 STEMI needs fast reperfusion, often a cath lab

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

ST up? Get the cath lab up!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: A hospital nurse has a TB skin test read at 48 to 72 hours. Which result is positive?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #296!

🫁 TB skin test day. Do you measure the redness or the bump?

This is a HIGH-YIELD infection control question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Induration of 10 mm

🧠 Rationale: Read the test in 48 to 72 hours.

Measure only the raised, hard area (induration), not the redness.

For health care workers, 10 mm or more is positive.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: TB Skin Test (Mantoux)

📏 Positive Results:

🔹 5 mm or more: HIV, immunosuppressed, close contacts

🔹 10 mm or more: health care workers, recent immigrants

🔹 15 mm or more: no known risk factors

💉 How It Is Given:

🔹 Intradermal injection on the inner forearm

🔹 Forms a small bleb

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Do not rub or cover the site

✅ Measure induration in mm

✅ Positive test needs a chest X-ray

⚠️ Remember:

🔹 Positive test shows exposure, not always active disease

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Feel the bump, ignore the blush!

photos.question: Which finding suggests hyperglycemia rather than hypoglycemia?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #297!

🩸 High sugar or low sugar? Can you tell them apart?

This is a HIGH-YIELD endocrine question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Increased thirst and urination

🧠 Rationale: High glucose spills into the urine and pulls water with it.

This causes polyuria, then thirst (polydipsia).

Shakiness, sweating, clammy skin and hunger point to hypoglycemia.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Hyperglycemia vs Hypoglycemia

📈 Hyperglycemia Signs:

🔹 Polyuria, polydipsia, polyphagia

🔹 Hot, dry skin

🔹 Blurred vision and fatigue

📉 Hypoglycemia Signs:

🔹 Shaky, sweaty, cool and clammy

🔹 Hunger and anxiety

🔹 Confusion if severe

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Check glucose first

✅ Low and awake: 15 g fast carbs, recheck in 15 min

✅ High: follow insulin orders, check ketones

🚑 When to Escalate:

🔹 Unconscious client: glucagon or IV dextrose

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Hot and dry, sugar high. Cold and clammy, need some candy!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: Which action helps protect the suture line after cleft lip repair in an infant?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #298!

👶 Fresh cleft lip repair. How should this baby lie?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pediatric question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Position the infant on the back or side

🧠 Rationale: Lying prone lets the face rub the bed and damage the repair.

Back or side lying protects the suture line.

Avoid pacifiers and anything that puts tension on the lip.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Cleft Lip Repair

🍼 Feeding:

🔹 Special nipples or syringe feeding as ordered

🔹 Burp often, they swallow air

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Elbow restraints to keep hands away

✅ No pacifiers or straws

✅ Clean the suture line as ordered

✅ Manage pain and crying

⚠️ Watch For:

🔹 Redness or drainage at the site

🔹 Signs of aspiration with feeds

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Lip repair? Baby faces the sky, not the bed!

photos.question: The nurse asks a client to shrug both shoulders against resistance. Which cranial nerve is being tested?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #299!

🧠 Shrug your shoulders. Which cranial nerve just did that?

This is a HIGH-YIELD neuro question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — CN XI, accessory

🧠 Rationale: CN XI moves the trapezius and sternocleidomastoid.

Test it with shoulder shrugs and turning the head against resistance.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Cranial Nerve Testing

🔹 Quick Tests:

🔹 CN V: clench jaw, light touch on face

🔹 CN VII: smile, raise eyebrows

🔹 CN XI: shrug shoulders, turn head

🔹 CN XII: stick out tongue

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Compare left and right sides

✅ Report new weakness right away

⚠️ Red Flag:

🔹 Sudden one-sided weakness can mean stroke

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Eleven helps you shrug and say 'I don't know!'

photos.question: A client has dysphagia after a stroke. Which action helps prevent aspiration during meals?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #300!

🍽️ Stroke client at mealtime. One move keeps food out of the lungs.

This is a HIGH-YIELD safety question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Tuck the chin when swallowing

🧠 Rationale: Tucking the chin helps protect the airway.

Tilting the head back opens the airway and raises aspiration risk.

Straws and thin liquids move too fast for a weak swallow.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Aspiration Prevention

⚠️ Signs of Aspiration:

🔹 Coughing or choking with meals

🔹 Wet, gurgly voice

🔹 Fever or crackles later

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Swallow screen before any food

✅ Sit upright at 90 degrees

✅ Thickened liquids as ordered

✅ Small bites, unaffected side

✅ Stay upright 30 minutes after meals

🩺 Team:

🔹 Speech therapy evaluates swallowing

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Chin down, food down!
